sections.heading: Quick review

lines.en: This is my colleague, a woman.

sections.note: Say each phrase aloud before you hear the English.

sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.en: Do you have a big family?
Yes, I have a brother and a sister.
She's a doctor, and her husband is an engineer.
My brother is a student, and his name is Yusuf.
And where are your father and mother?
My father and mother are in Lagos.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. A friend asks Ridhwan about his family.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.note: Add hu to the end of a noun to say his, and haa to say her. Ismuhu means his name, ismuhaa means her name. Notice that brother, akh, becomes akhoo before an ending, as in akhooka, your brother.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root seen, ain, daal, meaning happiness

lines.en: fortunate, the one made happy. Also a name

sections.note: You know faa-il, the doer, maf-al, the place, and maf-ool, the one the action is done to. Today's new pattern is fa-eel, which often describes a quality. You already heard it in fursa sa-eeda, a happy chance.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: Do you have a big family?
Model answer: Yes, I have a big family.
Where are your father and mother?
Model answer: My father and mother are in Nigeria.
Model answer: His name is Ahmad, and he's a programmer.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
